articleTitle: Using Artificial Intelligence Tools in Advertising Product Development
publicationTitle: 2025 Communication Strategies in Digital Society Seminar (ComSDS)
abstract: Digital technologies and tools are becoming increasingly embedded in all areas of life in today's digital society. The field of advertising is no exception, with innovative resources, in particular artificial intelligence, being actively integrated to create personalised and effective communication campaigns. In the framework of this study, the authors have analysed and systematised the theoretical background and practical solutions for the development of advertising products using artificial intelligence technologies.

articleTitle: Visual Inclusive Communication of Socially-Oriented Nonprofit Organizations on Social Media
publicationTitle: 2025 Communication Strategies in Digital Society Seminar (ComSDS)
abstract: In the context of the growing influence of social media as a primary platform for communication and public opinion formation, socially oriented nonprofit organizations increasingly leverage these digital channels to fulfill their socially significant objectives. This study formulates an operational definition of visual inclusive communication and tests a methodological framework for evaluating visual content in terms of its inclusivity. Visual inclusive communication is conceptualized as the intersection of social representation, grounded in principles of equality and non-discrimination, and technological adaptation, ensuring accessibility and multimodality in digital environments. The study develops and empirically validates an evaluative methodology for assessing inclusivity in visual media communication. The research focuses on the visual media strategies of the St. Petersburg Association of Parents of Disabled Children (GAOORDI), analyzing its visual content against the proposed criteria for inclusive representation. The methodological framework integrates critical semiotic analysis, content analysis, and discourse analysis, facilitating a comprehensive assessment of inclusivity in media discourse. The analytical approach is based on the Visual Discourses of Disability (ViDD) model, which operates along two key axes: Perspective/Personalization and Enabling/Disabling. A scoring system is applied to categorize images according to their adherence to inclusive representation principles, examining factors such as subject portrayal, audience engagement, and the rhetorical role of visual elements in shaping public perception. The findings demonstrate that inclusive visual communication strategies enhance audience engagement, dismantle stereotypes, and foster social integration. The study underscores the transformative power of visual media in overcoming perceptual barriers and strengthening public trust. By proposing a structured evaluation methodology, this research offers a practical tool for optimizing visual communication strategies in nonprofit organizations, ensuring their alignment with evolving digital media paradigms and the core principles of equity and social justice. The empirical testing of this methodology confirms that GAOORDI’s visual media communication can be characterized as inclusive.

articleTitle: Engaging Audiences in Transmedia Communication in the Context of the Digital Technology Frontier
publicationTitle: 2025 Communication Strategies in Digital Society Seminar (ComSDS)
abstract: Technological progress has contributed to the emergence of a digital mediacommunication environment, in which the structure of communication connections and interactions of its actors is being transformed. First, the production process, which involves the creation of media content in a certain way, as well as the practices of its storage, distribution and promotion, is subject to transformation. Secondly, we are talking about the resource potential and opportunities of the actors of mediacommunication interaction to realize their own goals by entering into communication. Network models of digital mediacommunication in the convergent media environment have actualized the research framework of media content distribution and production, as well as the resource potential of its perception by the audience in the context of the theory of transmedia communication, with its inherent character of interdiscursiveness and intermediality. But transmedia communication is carried out within a certain limit of digital technologies, which is provided by the modern technological development of the mediacommunication environment. Therefore, in the article the author makes an attempt to consider not only the technological capabilities of various platforms in the digital mediacommunication environment as a prerequisite for the emergence of transmedia communication. In the article the author describes the semiotic potential of media platforms, which are structural elements of the process of transmedia communications.

articleTitle: Remote Electronic Voting as an Institutionalized Format of Digital Communication between the Government and Society
publicationTitle: 2025 Communication Strategies in Digital Society Seminar (ComSDS)
abstract: The article discusses remote electronic voting (REV) as an institutionalized format of digital political communication that ensures interaction between the government and society in the context of the digital transformation of public administration. Key characteristics of REV, its historical evolution, regulatory and legal foundations, and institutional mechanisms for implementation are analyzed. Special attention is given to axiological aspects, including value orientations of democratic participation, transparency, and electoral fairness. It is concluded that the effectiveness of institutionalizing REV as a mechanism for communication between the government and society in modern Russia requires improvement of legal regulation, enhancement of information security standards, and development of tools to increase citizens’ digital trust.

articleTitle: Specificity of Manipulative Technologies in the Media Space
publicationTitle: 2025 Communication Strategies in Digital Society Seminar (ComSDS)
abstract: The article examines the specificity of manipulative technologies used in the media space, and analyzes the methods and techniques of manipulation used in various forms of media. An assessment is given of how various media formats use manipulative technologies to influence the audience, examples are analyzed demonstrating the influence of media on the formation of public opinion. Based on qualitative and quantitative methods of content analysis, recommendations for critical perception of information are developed and practical advice on improving the media literacy of the population is offered.

articleTitle: The Comic as a Reflection of the Communicant’s Culture: a Case Study of a Publication for Professional IT Community
publicationTitle: 2025 Communication Strategies in Digital Society Seminar (ComSDS)
abstract: Resorting to the comic is one of the most popular speech tools in the Internet editions for professional IT community. The comic is regarded as an integral part of the professional culture of an IT specialist. It increases the effectiveness of contact establishment, intimizes communication, lets one express his attitude, allows one to manifest his axiological position and strengthen solidarity with other members of the community. A member of the community can regard his own group as from the part of an outsider, which contributes to the additional solidarization of community participants and the building of a more adequate professional worldview.

articleTitle: Application and Development of In-Vehicle Digital Communication Technology
publicationTitle: 2025 Communication Strategies in Digital Society Seminar (ComSDS)
abstract: In-vehicle digital communication technology plays a crucial role in the modern automotive industry by supporting real-time data interaction between vehicles and the external environment, which enhances driving safety, efficiency and user experience. This article discusses the fundamentals of in-vehicle digital communication technologies, key technologies (e.g., CAN bus, Ethernet, V2X, 5G/6G, Bluetooth, NFC, and UWB), and their applications in current and future self-driving vehicles. The article analyzes how the technologies are implemented, the challenges they face, and the future direction of development.

articleTitle: Communication Strategy of AI-application in News Reporting: Human Values or Technological Effectiveness?
publicationTitle: 2025 Communication Strategies in Digital Society Seminar (ComSDS)
abstract: The paper examines trends in the use of artificial intelligence technologies for news journalism. The axiological approach has been applied as a scientific framework. The axiological approach allows us to examine the additional value load created by artificial intelligence technologies in modern news. The empirical study tests the ability of the audience to determine the authorship of news materials generated by ChatGPT-prompt. The study verifies basic value arguments in justifying or discrediting the use of artificial intelligence in journalism, such as trust, emotionality, diversity, speed, etc. The main research method is a survey with a questionnaire ($\text{N}=108$). The main problems of using artificial intelligence technologies in news journalism and the associated risks of reducing trust in the media as sources of information are revealed. Empirical data collected through a survey indicate a relatively high level of uncertainty and inconsistency of answers, which corresponds to the initial stage of technology development.

articleTitle: Capitalization of Attention, Digital Labor and Digital Exploitation of Internet Audiences in the Transition to a Platform Society
publicationTitle: 2025 Communication Strategies in Digital Society Seminar (ComSDS)
abstract: The article discusses modern theoretical approaches to understanding the capitalization of attention and digital labor in the emerging platform society. The article substantiates the concept of attention as a valuable asset for which various digital platforms compete. The authors pay special attention to the phenomenon of digital exploitation of Web users, emphasizing the ambiguous character of the economic nature of exchange in the current state of platform society.

articleTitle: The Communication Paradigm of Modern Advertising: From Goods to Emotions
publicationTitle: 2025 Communication Strategies in Digital Society Seminar (ComSDS)
abstract: The digital age is shaping a new type of society: analog technologies are being replaced by digital technologies, and analog society is turning into a digital society. However, a person's need to experience a unique experience in the process of communicating with a brand can only be realized in an analog world. The paradigm of experiential marketing is based on the emotional impact and formation of unique consumer experiences using: experience, exchange, extension, emphasis, empathy capital, emotional touchpoints, emic / etic process. Audiovisual communication products use the language of cinema, which has in its arsenal such an emotive element as a movie plot. By emotion genic elements of a communication product, we mean those units of the form and content of a communication product endowed with a special meaning, capable of evoking an emotional response from the viewer, projected onto the advertised object. Sensory communication products affect all the senses: sight, hearing, taste, smell and tactility. Immersive communication products allow the brand's audience to be not just its end recipient, but its accomplice and co-creator. The purpose of the research is to actualize the ways and technologies of forming a unique consumer experience and emotions in a new marketing paradigm. The authors adhere to a semiotic approach to the study of brand communication with consumers, the analysis of audiovisual communication products is based on the semiotics of cinema. According to Y. Lotman, the analysis of sensory and immersive communication products is based on the non-verbal semiotics of G. Kreidlin. The method of semiotic analysis is used as a method for investigating the empirical base.

articleTitle: Digital Media Communication Strategy on the Rights of Persons with Disability in Russia
publicationTitle: 2025 Communication Strategies in Digital Society Seminar (ComSDS)
abstract: IT technologies and digital media development influence to understand the actual situation in a particular area in a certain period and the formation of a new state disability policy. The social policy of the Russian state is aimed at involving socially vulnerable groups of the population in all spheres of social life. The methodological basis of the study is devoted to the problems of social inclusion of people with disabilities, ideology of independent living and models of disability policy (R. Drake). Thus, the study objective was to explore of legislative and regulatory support, assessments by disabled people of the to lead their rights of involving digital media. The study was conducted during two step: pilot study July 29 – August 11, 2023 and main study December 11, 2024 – 31 January, 2025. The results demonstrated that digital field is a reflection of what is happening in offline reality. The positive assessment of persons with disability, representations about the rights of persons with disabilities are initiated in connection with their gross violations and actions of the authorities in Russia digital media communication. However, the institutional processes of the digital field are at the stage of formation.

articleTitle: AI-Driven Personalization in Organizational Communication
publicationTitle: 2025 Communication Strategies in Digital Society Seminar (ComSDS)
abstract: This study investigates the transformative impact of artificial intelligence on corporate communications, focusing on AI-powered personalization systems in business environments. Through a systematic literature review (2019-2024), the research establishes an empirical framework for evaluating these systems’ technological infrastructure. The findings reveal distinct sector-specific performance variations: the retail sector showing 58% enhanced engagement metrics, while B2B segments demonstrated 28% improvement in key performance indicators. The technological foundation comprises machine learning algorithms, natural language processing frameworks, and high-performance computing systems enabling real-time personalization. The methodology integrates the adaptive personalization framework (APF) with the multidimensional personalization model (MPM) to elucidate machine learning mechanisms. This framework supports user profiling, navigation optimization, and behavioral pattern modification, secured through distributed ledger technologies. Empirical analysis reveals the complementarity between AI and human capabilities. While AI systems excel in response velocity (mean: 4.92), human interactions demonstrate superior responsiveness (5.27) and professional competency metrics (5.32 vs. 4.87), suggesting the optimality of a hybrid model. The study culminates in a conceptual framework balancing communication scalability with personalized relevance while adhering to ethical imperatives of data protection, algorithmic fairness, and transparency protocol.

articleTitle: Corporate Citizen as a Subject of Social Architecture: Digital Mediapresence Analysis
publicationTitle: 2025 Communication Strategies in Digital Society Seminar (ComSDS)
abstract: Digital technologies development caused network society evolvement which is characterized by “networkisation” of public policies and business activities (Castells, 1996, 1998, 2000; Smorgunov, 2018; Kurochkin, 2011). People’s socialization process is deploying either offline or online. Social architecture activities in the form of social investment programmes and projects reveal itself in compliance with it in digital mediascene and offline either. The focus of the article is made on the analysis of key social investment programmes and projects of corporate citizens in the Russian digital media space, outlining their leading stories and senses.

articleTitle: Transforming Brand Communication: The Impact of Artificial Intelligence, Virtual Reality, and Augmented Reality in the Digital Era
publicationTitle: 2025 Communication Strategies in Digital Society Seminar (ComSDS)
abstract: The advent of Artificial Intelligence (AI), Virtual Reality (VR), and Augmented Reality (AR) technologies is revolutionizing the landscape of brand communication. This paper explores how these technologies are reshaping the strategies brands employ to engage with their audiences, enhance customer experiences, and foster brand loyalty. By analyzing current applications and emerging trends, the study highlights the transformative potential of AI in personalizing communication, VR in creating immersive brand experiences, and AR in bridging the physical and digital worlds. The findings suggest that integrating AI, VR, and AR into brand communication strategies not only enhances interactivity and engagement but also provides brands with valuable data insights to refine their approaches. This research contributes to the understanding of digital communication paradigms and offers practical recommendations for brands seeking to leverage these technologies effectively.

articleTitle: Digital Tools for Combating Corruption (The Case of China)
publicationTitle: 2025 Communication Strategies in Digital Society Seminar (ComSDS)
abstract: The purpose of the study is to identify the features of digital anti-corruption technologies. The object of the study was the digital anti-corruption system implemented in China. The methodology of studying the potential and difficulties faced by these technologies in the fight against corruption is based on the methods of case studies, expert interviews and analysis of secondary data. The results of the study capture the degree of effectiveness of digital anticorruption technologies.

articleTitle: Design of Wireless Communication System in Mine
publicationTitle: 2025 Communication Strategies in Digital Society Seminar (ComSDS)
abstract: With the rapid development of communication technology, the introduction of wireless communication in some limited areas, such as tunnels, semi-buried highways, underground car parks, mines and other scenarios, gradually reflects the development prospects of the scheme. This paper mainly focuses on the space-constrained mine environment, proposes the use of SC-FDE technology for wireless communication in mines, and investigates the timing synchronisation and frequency bias estimation algorithms. In order to solve the synchronisation problem of SC-FDE communication scheme, the characteristics of ZC sequence and the influence of frequency deviation on its correlation are analysed. In order to resist the influence of frequency bias and noise in the mine channel, this paper proposes a timing synchronisation algorithm based on the improved ZC sequence on the basis of the inter-correlation synchronisation algorithm, and at the same time gives a frequency synchronisation algorithm based on two iterations of phase difference to compensate for the frequency bias, and carries out the simulation analysis of the proposed algorithm on the basis of the channel model established in this paper.

articleTitle: Streaming Services as a Promotional Instrument within the Digital Media Environment
publicationTitle: 2025 Communication Strategies in Digital Society Seminar (ComSDS)
abstract: The advent of streaming technologies can be ascribed to the innovative nature of the content they offer, the popularity of which has increased dramatically in recent years. The objective of this study is to provide a theoretical framework for integrating streaming platforms into the broader concept of promoting an organisation in today’s digital landscape. The article elucidates the main characteristics of streaming communications, explores ways to integrate them into an enterprise promotion programme and offers recommendations on how to effectively incorporate streaming platforms into an enterprise promotional strategy.

articleTitle: Virtualization of Communication in Metaverses: Key Trends and Prospects
publicationTitle: 2025 Communication Strategies in Digital Society Seminar (ComSDS)
abstract: The article examines the key trends in the virtualization of communication within metaverses, which drive the transformation of social interactions in digital environments. With the advancement of virtual and augmented reality (VR/AR), artificial intelligence (AI), and blockchain technologies, new mechanisms of social, professional, and economic cooperation are emerging, characterized by interactivity, immersion, and decentralization. The study analyzes seven fundamental trends, including the mediation of communication through digital avatars, the gamification of communicative interactions, the hybridization of physical and virtual communication environments, the economization of digital communication practices, the decentralization of socio-communicative processes, as well as the increasing asynchronicity and permanence of digital communication. The findings of the study demonstrate that metaverses not only reshape traditional forms of social communication but also foster the development of new models of digital identity, economic activity, and collective governance.

articleTitle: Media Strategy of Political Identity Building in the Digital Society: The Case of Euronews
publicationTitle: 2025 Communication Strategies in Digital Society Seminar (ComSDS)
abstract: The paper examines the problem of constructing European identity using digital media. Identity is defined as a set of ideas about a person’s place in society, the values and behavioral models that are established on the basis of correlating oneself with socially significant cultural reference points and role functions in the public sphere, with social institutions and relationships. In a digital society, digital media play an important role in creating political identity. The report uses a case study method to study the contribution of Euronews to the creation of European identity. The report concludes that a pan-European identity is gradually strengthening, but the role of Euronews in this process is contradictory and is assessed as rather a negative one.

articleTitle: Development of Tools for Studying the Practices of Using AI by Residents of a Megalopolis: Methodology and Analysis
publicationTitle: 2025 Communication Strategies in Digital Society Seminar (ComSDS)
abstract: There are many aspects of social interaction associated with the use of artificial intelligence technologies in everyday life, which makes the study of such practices among residents of a megalopolis an important area of research. In a megalopolis, the use of AI covers a variety of areas, which requires an integrated approach to data collection and analysis. The article discusses a methodological approach to studying the practices of using artificial intelligence (AI) technologies among the residents of a megalopolis, based on automated analysis of open data. Based on the pilot study, key sources of information and their analytical potential for further in-depth study are evaluated. The authors present a combined method aimed at identifying the differentiation of practices in the application of AI. To study the practices of using AI, an approach was applied that includes automated data collection and analysis: open data research using parsing and machine learning methods, which allows us to identify trends and features of the use of AI. Main data sources for the analysis include: Telegram bots and channels dedicated to AI; Mobile app from the Store Market using AI technology, the company profiles on Google Maps and Yandex.Maps that demonstrate the use of AI, social networks, and media outlets that publish information about AI. As part of the pilot testing, data was collected from these sources. The results confirmed that each source provides valuable data for the analysis of AI-based tools and services. This confirms the expediency of using these sources to identify differences in AI usage practices. The pilot study showed that automated data analysis technologies can be effective for studying the practices of using AI in a megacity. In the future, it is planned to conduct a more in-depth data analysis to identify patterns and trends in the use of AI technologies among various social groups in the metropolis.

articleTitle: Breaking News as a Factor of Media Temporality in Telegram
publicationTitle: 2025 Communication Strategies in Digital Society Seminar (ComSDS)
abstract: One of the least studied phenomena in communication theory is social time in cyberspace. Although social time has been a subject of study since the classics of twentieth-century sociology and remains of interest today, there is a notable lack of both foundational work and empirical research applied to the online environment. Breaking news emerges as an important factor influencing the temporal dynamics of online communication. We hypothesise that breaking news has a significant impact on the temporal characteristics of interactions in digital spaces. Specifically, we investigate the frequency of breaking news and the resulting communication dynamics. To enhance the comparability of our study data, we analysed how breaking news influences the temporality of communication within three thematic areas across Telegram channels

articleTitle: Intelligent Communication Applications in Mine Power Management
publicationTitle: 2025 Communication Strategies in Digital Society Seminar (ComSDS)
abstract: The coal mine power system is an indispensable infrastructure in the coal mine production process, which is directly related to the safe, efficient and sustainable production of the coal mine. With the development of the coal mine power system, the role of intelligent communication technology in mine power management is becoming more and more important. This article lists several key roles of intelligent communication technology in mine power management, including real-time monitoring and data transmission, intelligent power dispatching, remote control and unattended operation, intelligent control and fault diagnosis. Intelligent communication technology will change the dispatching and integration methods of coal mine power systems, and the communication technology in coal mine power systems will be more intelligent and energy efficiency will be higher.

articleTitle: Visual Storytelling as a Strategy for Online Political Communication
publicationTitle: 2025 Communication Strategies in Digital Society Seminar (ComSDS)
abstract: The article examines the perception of visual content within politicized virtual Russian-speaking communities on social media, focusing specifically on platforms such as VKontakte, YouTube, and Telegram. The study positions visual storytelling as a powerful tool in online political communication, emphasizing its role in eliciting emotional responses and simplifying the transmission of complex information. The research uses a mixed-methods approach, combining discourse analysis and focus group studies. Discourse analysis is used to identify and analyze the narrative strategies employed within Russian-language virtual political communities. A series of focus groups were conducted to assess the effectiveness of different narrative forms among different age groups. The focus group sessions used stimulus materials to identify visual narratives that have the potential to influence the formation of political trust. The results show that certain visual materials are more effective in engaging audiences and shaping political perceptions. These materials use emotional appeal and narrative simplicity to enhance their impact. The study concludes by highlighting the importance of tailoring visual storytelling strategies to specific audience demographics in order to maximize their effectiveness in political communication.

articleTitle: Study on the Effect of Bit Error Rate on the Performance of Digital Communication System
publicationTitle: 2025 Communication Strategies in Digital Society Seminar (ComSDS)
abstract: Bit error rate is an important index to evaluate the performance of digital communication system. In this paper, the effects of bit error rate on signal transmission and reception performance are studied, and the main factors are understood by analyzing the operating environment and signal processing methods. This paper also provides a solution to effectively reduce the bit error rate, and discusses the change law of the bit error rate in different scenarios.

articleTitle: Artificial Intelligence as a Tool for Transforming Communications Formats in Higher Education
publicationTitle: 2025 Communication Strategies in Digital Society Seminar (ComSDS)
abstract: Artificial intelligence is emerging as a significant tool for transforming the educational process, including the forms and modes of communication in higher education. This study aims to explore the role of AI in reshaping communication formats, defined here as both the channels of interaction between participants and their symbolic content. The methodology encompasses focus groups, secondary data analysis, and expert interviews. The findings outline key directions of transformation and highlight the prospects for the application of AI in education.

articleTitle: The Eye-Tracking Analysis of Framing Effects in the Regional Environmental Agenda through Mass Media and Social Media Communication Strategies
publicationTitle: 2025 Communication Strategies in Digital Society Seminar (ComSDS)
abstract: This study presents the results of an eye-tracking analysis of framing effects in the regional environmental agenda of mass media and social media. The paper identifies seven types of frames and conducts an eye-tracking analysis of the attention of three groups of respondents (aged 18-30 years old) to the identified types of frames based on the “all fix” (units) and “fix time” (ms) indicators. The eye-tracking analysis revealed the leading types of frames (morality/environmental education, human impact, threat) and the respondents’ maximum attention to the “main text” area of interest.

articleTitle: Applications of Blockchain Technology in the Educational Activities of Universities
publicationTitle: 2025 Communication Strategies in Digital Society Seminar (ComSDS)
abstract: The paper considers the key applications of blockchain technology in the educational environment of universities. Digitalization has promoted the introduction of new digital forms of student learning; artificial intelligence, big data, and distributed ledger technologies are widely used in educational processes. The topic of implementation and use of blockchain technologies in the processes of student learning is of scientific and practical interest, so it requires detailed consideration. The main purpose of the study is to consider the key areas of using blockchain in the educational activities of universities, to highlight the advantages and disadvantages of using this technology, legal aspects of using artificial intelligence in the educational process. When doing the research, we used the methods of desk review of works written within the framework of this topic, as well as the method of comparative analysis, interpretation of law, comprehensive analysis of statistical reports, analytical data, surveys, reports and conference proceedings. The study concluded that the most promising areas of using blockchain technologies in the educational activities of universities are as follows: the creation of digital certificates on the results of training; ensuring the monitoring of academic performance; sharing materials created on different resources; identification; document storage; confirmation of authorship; the use of smart contracts for the automation of learning processes.

articleTitle: Digital Needs of Citizens: Experience of Evaluation of Urban Digital Services in Groups of Young Parents and Disabled People
publicationTitle: 2025 Communication Strategies in Digital Society Seminar (ComSDS)
abstract: This article is part of the interim results of a large scientific project «Study of the social impact of electronic interaction between citizens and authorities in Canton Petersburg on the example of urban digital services», conducted under the auspices of the Russian Science Foundation & St. Petersburg Science Foundation. The article aims to demonstrate one of the approaches for assessing the social impact of urban digital services through an analysis of meeting the digital needs of citizens. The theoretical framework that allows us to consider digital interactions as social communications, mutually beneficial for service providers and consumers, was the concept of social capital, that can occur in interactions when using digital services. Two social groups were selected as the objects for research of the digital needs of citizens: parents with children of preschool age and the disabled; as a digital service with elements of personalized service provision, the mini-application «I live here» was analyzed on the platform of VKontakte, which is part of the Ecosystem of urban services «Digital Petersburg». Conclusions were drawn on aspects that affect satisfaction with services, and the concept of social performance was clarified. The areas identified for measuring the social impact of digital services are defined, taking into account further analysis of the digital needs of the population.

articleTitle: Development Trends of Regional Telegram Channels: Specifics of Audience Engagement
publicationTitle: 2025 Communication Strategies in Digital Society Seminar (ComSDS)
abstract: The aim of the article is to study the dynamics of regional Telegram channels development in the period of media system transformation in 2022-2024. The authors argue that the blocking of a number of social networks and the transition of the audience to other digital platforms caused a powerful influx of Telegram messenger audience. A comparative study of the development of 52 regional Telegram channels in Russia and Belarus allowed us to periodize the changes in the regional media space and draw conclusions about the reasons for the changes. Our research shows that many regional Telegram channels are in search of new communication strategies to work with their audiences. It was found that Telegram should serve not only as a one-way information channel, but also as a platform for creating engaging content. We argue that official media often cede leadership to Telegram channels with user-generated content built around publicizing the region’s trouble spots. The results confirm that the ongoing changes are quite dynamic and are rapidly reshaping the structure of the media market in the regions.

articleTitle: The Promoter’s Social Rating (on Example of Activity of Yaroslavl Region Public Chamber`s Members in Vkontakte Social Network)
publicationTitle: 2025 Communication Strategies in Digital Society Seminar (ComSDS)
abstract: The paper develops, substantiates, and tests a rating system for promoters of socio-political institutions in the digital environment using the example of the social network VKontakte. Based on desk research, a system of indicators has been developed for compiling this rating. The survey of experts not only allowed confirmation of this system of indicators, but also to supplement it with equalizing coefficients between these indicators. The developed method for rating promoters of socio-political institutions was tested in the assessment of members of the Public Chamber of Yaroslavl region. For this purpose, data were collected from their accounts. As a result, the features of digital communication were revealed, expressed in the promotion of this institution on the social network VKontakte by its members, and the audience’s reaction to them. Among the important conclusions, we can answer the following: 1) members of the civic Chamber do not consider themselves as its promoters; 2) the audience of the social network VKontakte reacts poorly to materials about the activities of the Public Chamber; 3) the rating allows one to accurately assess the activities of individual members of the Public Chamber and identify their various communication strategies in the digital space; 4) the revision of the promoter rating is optimal from the point of view of supplementing it with data on activity in other work formats.

articleTitle: Humans and Robots: Transformations of Professional Communication in the Digital Era
publicationTitle: 2025 Communication Strategies in Digital Society Seminar (ComSDS)
abstract: The current stage of technological progress is characterized by the widespread introduction of robots into the manufacturing and service industries. Robots are already performing complex tasks that were previously considered the prerogative of humans, and this trend continues to intensify. The article is devoted to the analysis of changes in professional communications under the influence of robotization and digital transformation. The paper examines the key problems arising from the introduction of robots as products of digital technology achievements into work processes and suggests ways to solve them. The task is to successfully integrate innovations into the professional environment for effective interaction between humans and machines. The research objective is to study the impact of robotics on professional communication and identify strategic approaches to adapting employees and organizations to new working conditions, taking into account various aspects of human-robot interaction. The conclusion is that the introduction of robots into work processes leads to significant changes in professional communications, which requires a new organization of the workflow and interpersonal interaction. Professional communication between humans and robots is becoming an important component of modern labor relations.

articleTitle: Content Strategies of Music Artists in the Digital Age of the Music Industry (by the Example of Russian Musical Artists)
publicationTitle: 2025 Communication Strategies in Digital Society Seminar (ComSDS)
abstract: In the context of the increasingly rapid digitalization that is prevalent in both the media and communications sectors, the music industry is undergoing significant changes that have a considerable impact on both the process of music creation and the methods and tools for its promotion. This article examines how Russian music artists are adapting their content strategies in the context of digital transformation, using social media to promote their creativity. The study focuses on the changes in music perception caused by the development of streaming platforms and algorithms, as well as on the research of artists’ content strategies.

articleTitle: Features of the Communication Process Between Humans and Neural Networks
publicationTitle: 2025 Communication Strategies in Digital Society Seminar (ComSDS)
abstract: Artificial intelligence technologies are increasingly permeating the modern world, and neural networks play a key role in this process. Their ability to perform machine learning and process large amounts of data opens up new horizons in many areas of human activity. However, despite the rapid development of this field, the issue of high-quality communication between humans and neural networks remains relevant and insufficiently studied. This paper is devoted to the study of communication between humans and neural networks in the context of their growing integration into various spheres of society. According to the results of the study, the peculiarities of communication between humans and neural networks were revealed. The results of the study demonstrate clear differences between the initial requests to neural networks and the final interpretation of their responses by users. Based on the collected data, the authors identified the key features of communication between humans and neural networks.

articleTitle: Legal Aspects of the Use of Artificial Intelligence in the Educational Environment of Universities
publicationTitle: 2025 Communication Strategies in Digital Society Seminar (ComSDS)
abstract: The article considers the legal aspects of the use of artificial intelligence in the educational process. In the era of total digitalization, the educational process has also started to use modern communication technologies on a regular basis. Artificial intelligence is widely used in universities and greatly facilitates the learning process, while solving many tasks of educators. The main purpose of the study is to highlight the advantages and disadvantages of using artificial intelligence in student learning and to propose measures to prevent legal risks arising from the digitalization of education in universities. The paper uses the methods of desk review of scientific research, analytical reviews, results of surveys of educators, reports and statistical data. It uses the method of comparative analysis and interpretation of law. As a result, the following advantages of using artificial intelligence in the educational process have been identified: automation of educational processes; personalized creation of educational materials; adaptation of educational material to particular students; round-the-clock interaction; interactive content; accessibility; analytics. Among the disadvantages the following are noted: imperfect technologies; violation of personal data security; responsibility and rights of artificial intelligence. Scientific novelty: based on the analysis, the main fields of using artificial intelligence in the educational process have been identified and supplemented: adaptive learning; gamification; robot creation; nano-learning; generation of educational material; online MOOC platforms with educational content; tutoring; introduction of information and consulting systems; automatic assessment of knowledge; customization of educational materials for individual characteristics; application of pre-trained artificial intelligence systems. The paper defines the tasks facing educators, which can be solved with the use of artificial intelligence. Practical significance: the analysis of legal risks that arise while using artificial intelligence in the process of teaching students can minimize these disadvantages and regulate at the legislative level the legal characteristics of the use of artificial intelligence at any stage of the educational process in higher education institutions.

articleTitle: Digital Communication Strategies for Coping with DeepFake Content Distribution
publicationTitle: 2025 Communication Strategies in Digital Society Seminar (ComSDS)
abstract: With the rapid development of generative artificial intelligence (AI) technology, DeepFake technology has triggered a wide-ranging discussion on authenticity of digital content and misuse of the technology worldwide. Although DeepFake technology has demonstrated positive applications in the fields of film and television entertainment, education, medical rehabilitation, and cultural heritage protection, its misuse has led to social problems such as reputation infringement, telecommunication fraud, and public opinion manipulation. Aiming at this status quo, this paper analyzes the existing detection means, including methods based on local texture and deep feature fusion, facial natural texture degree recognition, geometric feature analysis, and Generative Adversarial Network (GAN) adversarial detection, and explores their performances and shortcomings in recognition accuracy and generalization ability. At the same time, a multifaceted response strategy is proposed: creators are required to follow ethical protocols to embed digital watermarks, users are actively involved in monitoring through reporting mechanisms, platforms achieve content traceability and responsibility tracking through digital fingerprinting, and technicians optimize the multimodal detection model and promote open source and ease of use. This paper emphasizes the combination of technical means and institutional constraints to achieve multi-party collaboration to build a healthy and transparent digital communication ecosystem, and to jointly address the risk of DeepFake content dissemination.

articleTitle: Sociological Factors of Surgeons’ Professional Reputation Management (ANT Perspective)
publicationTitle: 2025 Communication Strategies in Digital Society Seminar (ComSDS)
abstract: The digital society, shaped by the Internet environment, has simplified individuals interactions by increasing information openness and reducing the costs associated with peripherality. As a result, traditional hierarchical social structures, such as the pyramid, are increasingly replaced by rhizomatic networks. These shifts have profound implications for social management, as professional reputation, which serves the base of credibility, transitions from a closed phenomenon to a critical determinant of success for both individuals and their organizations. This study offers a new framework for analyzing the professional reputations of surgeons, integrating methodology of the theory of cities (L. Boltanski, L. Thévenot, and E. Chiapello) and actor-network theory (J. Law). The study identifies that a surgeon’s professional reputation is a compromise among three value hierarchies —Reputation, Market, and Industrial—and explores how these factors manifest within both physical (“Euclidean”) and social spaces.

articleTitle: Strategies of Anti-Censorship Activism: Analysis of Discursive Dynamics in the Digital Environment
publicationTitle: 2025 Communication Strategies in Digital Society Seminar (ComSDS)
abstract: The paper analyzes the strategies and methods used by media activists in anti-censorship campaigns. It analyzes the key ways of creating content on the Internet, its influence on public opinion and the formation of narratives. The research methodology includes content analysis and case study. Expected results include defining key practices that contribute to the development of anti-censorship discourse in digital media.

articleTitle: Slow Communication and Slow PR in a Fast Digital World in the Focus of Web-text Design Problem
publicationTitle: 2025 Communication Strategies in Digital Society Seminar (ComSDS)
abstract: The article deals with the epistemology of modern communicative knowledge and general theory of public relations in the conditions of digital transformation and deep mediatization of social life. Based on authoritative works on the slow world, it is shown that the acceleration of social interactions with reliance on the technologies of the fast digital world generates a counter social demand for slow analog communications and, accordingly, for slow PR. The rapid consumption of news, advertising and PR information often leads to a superficial perception of messages, which contributes to the spread of misleading data and sensationalism. In this context, slow communication offers an alternative approach that focuses on in-depth analysis and thorough research of events. This is particularly important in a context where general social trust in “fast world” sources is diminishing with the inability of ordinary consciousness to identify texts generated by generative artificial intelligence. Continuing the logic of the researchers of the phenomenon of “slow journalism”, the authors introduce the concept of slow PR and reveal its characteristics in the conditions of digital transformation. Special attention is paid to the organization of Web texts in the plane of the gadget screen. The authors show that traditional texts of the slow world fit into the space of the fast digital world with the help of Web-design according to usability principles, which allows absorbing information volumes on any screen (computer display, smartphone, smart watch face, etc.). The technology of Web-text organization is based on the concept of a frame and slots that make up this frame. Allocation of frames and distribution of text fragments in the screen plane is possible only on the basis of understanding the semantic organization of traditional texts. This is the key to effective communication, eliminating the contradiction between the spaces of fast and slow worlds.

articleTitle: Eye Tracking for Digital Storytelling Content in Edutainment
publicationTitle: 2025 Communication Strategies in Digital Society Seminar (ComSDS)
abstract: Modern tainment technologies in education are implemented as “hybrid” or a cluster paradigm based on the leverage of certain entertainment elements into the learning process. A variety of digital storytelling content in edutainment encourages to study the effectiveness of its multimodality, including texts, visuals, videos and their combinations. New types of non-verbal research techniques, such as eye tracking, provide a deeper understanding of learners’ behavior, perception patterns and cognitive strategies during their interaction with educational material. Purpose of the study: to investigate the gaze patterns and cognitive strategies used by students when working with learning material consisting of text, visual and combined slides. Research methods: the eye movement tracking experiment using the infrared eye tracker and the post-interview follow-up. Results of the study: processing strategies for presentations containing visual and textual elements differed among students. Cognitive strategies for processing visual and textual elements consisted of multiple patterns and required different processing times. The findings will help educational professionals to structure digital narrative content based on typical gaze patterns and highlight perceptual strategies to make learning material more effective. Conclusions: learning eye tracking metrics such as fixation time, gaze return, average fixation, saccades and their amplitudes, etc., helps to improve digital narrative content based on content perception patterns and learners’ interest in the content, as well as content complexity and cognitive load.

articleTitle: Technological Transformations of Professional Communication in Society 5.0
publicationTitle: 2025 Communication Strategies in Digital Society Seminar (ComSDS)
abstract: The study is devoted to the analysis of the impact of technological transformations on professional communication in the context of Society 5.0. The authors consider the role of digital technologies such as artificial intelligence, cloud computing, virtual reality, social networks and messengers in changing the nature of professional interaction. The advantages were identified, including better opportunities for communication and collaboration, as well as increased work and training efficiency. At the same time, new challenges and risks related to the legal and ethical aspects of the issue were noted. Examples of successful projects demonstrate the practical application of digital technologies in a professional environment. The study objective is to analyze the impact of modern technological transformations on professional communication in the context of Society 5.0 development, as well as to assess their role in optimizing digital information exchange processes, improving work efficiency and interaction between specialists. Thus, the study showed that technological transformations have significant potential to optimize the processes of digital information exchange, increase work efficiency and strengthen interaction between specialists. However, successful implementation of these technologies requires considering and addressing the emerging challenges and risks.

articleTitle: HAMI: Hybrid Adaptive AutoML for IoT Intrusion Detection
publicationTitle: 2025 Communication Strategies in Digital Society Seminar (ComSDS)
abstract: the growth of IoT devices presents significant security challenges due to their diverse and dynamic environments. To address this, we developed HAMI, a novel intrusion detection system. Our method leverages the GIFS algorithm, which combines feature rankings from ensemble models with genetic algorithms to uncover subtle inter-feature correlations, enhancing detection accuracy. Additionally, we introduce GridSearchSMOTE, a technique that optimizes data balancing by evaluating various SMOTE variants through a meticulous grid search, ensuring optimal performance for each dataset. Empirical evaluations of HAMI show superior accuracy, achieving a 99% detection rate and reduced false positives, outperforming existing systems. These results underscore HAMI’s potential to significantly improve IoT network security by exploring its scalability and real-time detection capabilities.

articleTitle: News Distribution in the Digital Environment: The Growing Dependence on Platforms
publicationTitle: 2025 Communication Strategies in Digital Society Seminar (ComSDS)
abstract: This article argues that in an era of digital media marked by increased demands on journalists’ competencies, adaptation to digital platforms plays a crucial role in the creation and distribution of news. Drawing on 45 interviews with news workers at 15 leading publishing houses in Belarus conducted between 2023 and 2024, as well as secondary materials, the authors conclude that digital platforms create new dependencies in news production. The results reveal a number of interrelated challenges: lack of resources to produce content for a newspaper, website, and 4-5 digital platforms simultaneously; increased government control; outdated methods of communicating with audiences; the need to adapt to algorithmic demands; a significant increase in the popularity of clickbait; the need to counter fake news; and regulation of how media use artificial intelligence (AI). Using Belarus as a case study, we map the actors involved in the search for new content distribution strategies. The results show that the growing dependence on platforms is increasingly limiting publishers’ autonomy every year. We suggest that the era of digitalization requires more significant structural changes in journalism than those that have been implemented so far.

articleTitle: Artificial Intelligence: an Assistant or a Creator? Complex Analysis of Jewelry Community’s Professional Chat
publicationTitle: 2025 Communication Strategies in Digital Society Seminar (ComSDS)
abstract: Optimization of routine processes increases production efficiency. However, such a rapid disruption of habitual everyday processes prevents timely adaptation to new reality and creates preconditions for social instability. AI-based technologies are beginning to replace human resources, but a substantial number of people lack an understanding of alternatives for their efforts application. If previously there was just automation of production processes that did not affect sphere of creativity and did not affect decision-making areas, now there is a concern that the creative side of the profession will also be replaced. The jewelry profession is a creative profession with many bifurcation points at each stage. In this regard, the sphere can serve as a good example for understanding how people negotiate to coexist in changing socio-technological conditions. The article provides a qualitative study of comments from the expert community of jewelers and expert interview analisys on the topic of using artificial intelligence in the field of jewelry manufacturing. Jewelry art requires years of training: mastering skills in modeling (both digital and material), sketching, casting, soldering, metal rolling, stone work, enamel work, etc. Nowadays there are opportunities to transfer these skills to AI. The analysis covers expert comments for December 2024 and January 2025. Comments were clustered on the base of statements made. The most frequently mentioned theses were identified. The result is a diagram of a new social interaction as part of a potentially new social contract. (Abstract)

articleTitle: Using User Feedback to Measure the Social Impact of Urban Digital Services: A Case Study of the Unified Resident Card of Saint-Petersburg
publicationTitle: 2025 Communication Strategies in Digital Society Seminar (ComSDS)
abstract: The modern development of urban digital services greatly simplifies the interaction of citizens and authorities, making it urgent to find new approaches to analyze their effectiveness. The study examined user reviews of the Unified Map of St. Petersburg mobile application as a data source for evaluating the social effectiveness of electronic services. The main hypothesis is that user reviews are a significant indicator reflecting the satisfaction of citizens and the level of their involvement in the process of digital interaction. A parser was developed for the analysis, which collected more than 600 reviews from the Google Play Market platform. The collected data, which included text comments and user ratings, were processed, classified, and thematically modeled using the LDA (Latent Dirichlet Allocation) method. This allowed us to highlight key topics related to the functionality of the application, the quality of its implementation, the user-friendliness of the interface and user suggestions for its improvement. The analysis of user ratings revealed the most problematic and positive aspects of using the application. The official responses of the developers were also analyzed, which made it possible to assess the current level of feedback and interaction with citizens.

articleTitle: Platform Priorities of the Russian Blogosphere: Trends and Changes
publicationTitle: 2025 Communication Strategies in Digital Society Seminar (ComSDS)
abstract: the article is devoted to the study of the transformation of the blogosphere in Russia in the context of the transition of bloggers to domestic online platforms. This process became especially noticeable after the introduction of a number of legislative restrictions aimed at using foreign digital platforms. As a result, many bloggers were forced to adapt to the new conditions, choosing alternative platforms for communicating with subscribers. This study addresses the issues of opinion transmission and information perception in the context of modern political and social realities. The article identifies trends in the adaptation of bloggers to new conditions associated with the transition to domestic online platforms. The empirical basis of the study is the results of a comparative analysis of 15 cases of bloggers switching from the international YouTube platform to the domestic RuTube. Representatives of different segments of the blogosphere have been selected: from popular video bloggers to micro-influencers broadcasting content of various subjects. This allowed us to cover a wide range of formats and approaches to content creation, as well as identify common patterns in the process of adapting content creators to new business conditions. The results of the study will help to understand how bloggers adapt to new conditions and what communication strategies they use to maintain communication with their audience.

articleTitle: Factors Increasing Place Attractiveness for Residential Mobility of Digital Nomads
publicationTitle: 2025 Communication Strategies in Digital Society Seminar (ComSDS)
abstract: The digital economy has had a profound and multifaceted impact on the work of professionals in almost all industries. This has led to significant changes in the form of changes in the skills and competencies required of modern professionals (increased demand for digital skills, focus on soft skills, continuous learning), changes in the nature of work (remote work and flexible schedules, automation and robotization of routine tasks, collaboration and networking among professionals), and changes in the structure and transformation of the labor market. Existing occupations, increased competition in the context of globalization of the labor market, and the emergence of new occupations related to the development and implementation of new technologies have led to changes in the structure of the labor market. This includes the transformation of existing professions and increased competition against the backdrop of the globalization of the labor market and the emergence of new professions related to the development and implementation of new technologies. The COVID-19 pandemic has accelerated the shift to remote work, exposing people of all ages, professions, and income levels to the possibility of living in one area and working in another. As a result, highly mobile professionals have emerged, seeking the best place to live and work, using flexible financial instruments, and performing their duties online. This paper explores the factors contributing to the increasing appeal of residence for digital nomads. It examines theoretical models of stakeholder involvement in the development of an ecosystem for digital nomads and provides a clarification of the term “digital nomad.” The analysis of ratings and rankings of the most suitable cities for this social category identifies the key criteria they use when selecting a place to live. The authors of this study propose a comprehensive approach for attracting digital nomads to the region, drawing from positive international experiences. This approach encompasses work on economic, social, infrastructural, administrative, and legislative factors. A significant focus has been placed on the particularities of Russian regions, with the objective of enhancing their appeal to this particular demographic.

articleTitle: Media Branding: Modifying Digital Communications of IT Companies
publicationTitle: 2025 Communication Strategies in Digital Society Seminar (ComSDS)
abstract: Digital media branding is a powerful tool that can modify strategic communications. This process makes it possible to move from passive dissemination of information to active formation of brand perception and establishment of long-term relationships with the audience in a digital environment, including the formation of a cohesive and loyal community around the company. This is especially relevant for companies whose content involves the inclusion of a specific target audience in communication, such as the IT community, for example. Strategic decisions on transformation and changes in media branding are influenced by various factors: public mood, ‘consumer portrait’, a set of consumer identities, the pace of technological change and others. Taking into account these parameters and operational monitoring of their changes helps brands to form a clear vision of themselves in the eyes of their audiences. This article explores aspects reflecting the coordinated use of various media platforms in a digital environment, ways to build trust in the brand and increase its competitiveness while maintaining a sustainable and multidimensional brand image. The authors of the study offer a comprehensive approach to analysing media branding as a process of forming a holistic and effective approach to strategic communications in the modern media landscape using the example of digital podcasts as one of the branding tools IT companies. In the contemporary context of content marketing, podcasts have evolved beyond a mere form of entertainment; they have become a sophisticated brand media platform. This transformation has enabled information technology (IT) companies to achieve several key objectives. Firstly, they have been able to enhance their image, secondly, they have been able to increase their niche influence, and thirdly, they have been able to establish a loyal community.

articleTitle: Digital Tools for Mythologizing the Past: Social Media and Neural Networks
publicationTitle: 2025 Communication Strategies in Digital Society Seminar (ComSDS)
abstract: The article is devoted to the study of the processes of mythologising the past in the digital age, where social media and neural networks are becoming key tools for the formation of collective memory. The authors analyse how digital technologies transform the ways of constructing historical narratives, blurring the boundaries between scientific knowledge and philistine notions of the past. Particular attention is paid to the role of socio-epistemic arenas where professional historians, history buffs, masses of Internet users and digital technologies interact as equals, creating new forms of historical knowledge. The article discusses examples of mythologising the past in social media such as Wikipedia, Internet memes, computer games and fanfics, and explores the influence of neural networks (GPT4, Midjourney, Gemini) on historical content creation. The authors emphasise that neural networks, capable of generating both reliable information and new myths, become active participants in the myth-making process. The article also touches upon the transformation of collective memory in the digital age, where media memory is becoming a new form of preservation and transmission of historical information. The authors conclude that digital technologies, on the one hand, open up new opportunities for the study and popularisation of history, and on the other hand, pose challenges to society in preserving historical accuracy in the context of mass myth-making. It concludes by emphasising the need to find a balance between the use of digital technologies and maintaining academic rigour in historical research.

articleTitle: Bloggers in the Modern Media Space: Agents of Socialization and Translators of Meanings
publicationTitle: 2025 Communication Strategies in Digital Society Seminar (ComSDS)
abstract: In the modern information society, characterized by the rapid development of digital technologies and the widespread spread of the Internet, the blogosphere has become an integral part of the media space. Bloggers, acting as creators and distributors of content, have a significant impact on digital communication, shaping public opinion, broadcasting values and constructing social reality. This article is devoted to the study of the role of bloggers in the modern media space, focusing on their functions as agents of socialization and translators of meanings. The purpose of this study is to identify media discourse strategies used by leading Russian bloggers and to reveal the specifics of their communication with the audience on significant dates for the Russian Federation. An important task was to consider the impact of their content on the processes of socialization. The paper uses the method of content analysis of publications by popular Russian bloggers, which allows to identify the dominant themes, narratives, stylistic features and value orientations broadcast in blogs. The findings of the research will enable to gain a better understanding of the processes of socialization in the digital era and establish the role of bloggers within the contemporary communication landscape.

articleTitle: Digital Analysis of the Environmental Media Texts Impact on the Emotional State of Young People through Media Communication Strategies
publicationTitle: 2025 Communication Strategies in Digital Society Seminar (ComSDS)
abstract: The human face registration and emotion recognition software enables the study of 6 basic emotions (enjoyment, surprise, sadness, fear, anger, and disgust) in the youth audience (18-30 years old) while analysing the impact of the mass media and social media information agenda on the industrial region environment. The digital facial movement coding system is studied when respondents are exposed to environmental media texts and when they are interviewed, revealing the intensity of the prevalence of negative basic emotions (sadness, fear).

articleTitle: Metacommunications: New Horizons of Professional Interaction in Virtual Worlds
publicationTitle: 2025 Communication Strategies in Digital Society Seminar (ComSDS)
abstract: Under the rapid growth and development of metaverses, professional communications are undergoing significant changes. The article explores a new phenomenon – metacommunications, which is a new format of professional interaction in virtual worlds. The study examines the distinctive characteristics of metacommunications, their technological, social and psychological aspects. It analyzes examples and cases of using metacommunications in business and educational environments. The study objective is to study the features of metacommunications and their impact on the professional world, to identify their potential and limitations compared with traditional forms of professional communication. It was established that metacommunications have significant potential for global interaction and acceleration of information exchange; however, there are certain limitations related to technological capabilities and perception of virtuality. The article presents practical recommendations for the effective implementation of metacommunication strategies and suggests directions for further research in this area. The study highlights the importance of studying metacommunications as a new phenomenon that plays a key role in the transformation of professional interactions in the digital era.
